text: Question: The nurse is caring for a group of assigned clients on the medical surgical unit. Which of the following clients should the nurse see first?
A. Client with a spinal cord injury who is flushed, diaphoretic.
B. Client with diabetes mellitus (type 2) who has a finger stick glucose level of 242 mg/dL.
C. Client with hyperparathyroidism with a calcium level of 11.5 mg/dL.
D. Client with angina complaining of a headache after receiving prescribed nitroglycerin.
Correct answer: A. Client with a spinal cord injury who is flushed, diaphoretic.
Topic: Prioritization & Delegation
notes: A flushed, diaphoretic client with a spinal cord injury suggests autonomic dysreflexia, a life-threatening emergency (severe hypertension, risk of stroke). The glucose of 242, calcium of 11.5, and a nitroglycerin headache are expected or only mildly abnormal and can wait.
(Answer key not on the slide; worked out with NCLEX reasoning, so check it against your class notes.)

text: Question: The nurse is caring for a group of assigned clients on the medical surgical unit. The UAP reports that a client is complaining of chest pain. Which of the following actions should the nurse perform first?
A. Ask the UAP to get a complete set of vital signs on the client.
B. Call the rapid response team.
C. Administer prescribed nitroglycerin sublingual tab.
D. Assess the client.
Correct answer: D. Assess the client.
Topic: Prioritization & Delegation
notes: Assessment comes first in the nursing process. The nurse must evaluate the chest pain before acting, then treat or escalate based on the findings.

text: Question: The nurse in the outpatient clinic is talking with a 42-year-old client who has hypertension and is receiving a loop diuretic. Which of the following statements by the client would require follow-up? Select all that apply.
A. “I should still follow my low-sodium diet.”
B. “I will stand slowly from a seated position.”
C. “I will increase my fluid intake each day to 5L.”
D. “I should weight myself once a month.”
E. “I will take the medication at the same time of the day, every day.”
Correct answers: C. “I will increase my fluid intake each day to 5L.”; D. “I should weight myself once a month.”
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Requires follow-up: drinking 5 L a day (fluid should not be pushed excessively and should be guided by the provider) and weighing once a month (diuretic clients should weigh daily to track fluid loss or gain). Low-sodium diet, standing slowly to prevent orthostatic hypotension, and a consistent daily dosing time are correct.
(Answer key not on the slide; worked out with NCLEX reasoning, so check it against your class notes.)

text: Question: The nurse in the outpatient clinic is caring for a 40-year-old client that is taking an ACE inhibitor. For each action listed, click to specify if the action is indicated or not indicated for the client. [In this app, select every action that is indicated.]
A. Teach the client to report if a dry cough occurs
B. Teach the client that the medication should be taken without food.
C. Advise the client to increase potassium intake.
D. Female clients who become pregnant should immediately notify the provider.
Correct answers: A. Teach the client to report if a dry cough occurs; D. Female clients who become pregnant should immediately notify the provider.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: ACE inhibitors commonly cause a dry cough (report it, the drug may need changing) and are teratogenic, so pregnancy must be reported at once. They cause potassium retention, so clients should NOT increase potassium intake, and most can be taken with or without food.
